questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

I remember my mother taking me to the stadium.

options.text: I remember being taken to the stadium by my mother.
I was taken to the stadium by mother that I remembered.
My mother remembered me taken to the stadium.
I was remembered being taken to the stadium by my mother

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "I remember my mother taking me to the stadium."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "me" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "taking" to "being taken" (passive gerund).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "my mother."
 
• Ensure the time phrase "to the stadium" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I remember being taken to the stadium by my mother."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"I was taken to the stadium by mother that I remembered." – Incorrect structure and meaning.
 
• **Option 3: **"My mother remembered me taken to the stadium." – Incorrect subject and verb form.
 
• **Option 4: **"I was remembered being taken to the stadium by my mother." – Incorrect structure and meaning.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Who did this?

options.text: This was done by who?
By who this was done?
By whom this was done?
By whom was this done?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **By whom was this done?**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

 
• **In the passive voice**, the structure should be: **Object + verb + Subject**

 
 
• Thus, **'whom' should be written before 'this'. **
 
 
 
• The **correct tense is simple past** as **'did' **has been** used in the sentence.**

 ​

Hence, the correct answer '*By whom was this done?'*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.**

The meeting was called off.

options.text: The meeting had been called off.
They called off the meeting.
Someone called off the meeting.
They were calling off the meeting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Someone called off the meeting**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 

__
 
• The sentence is in passive voice, which means the subject is receiving the action.
 
 
• **Passive** voice structure: Subject + verb + agent__
 
 
 
• __​__In the passive voice, the emphasis is on the receiver of the action (the meeting), and the entity performing the action (agent) is often omitted or placed in a prepositional phrase.
 
• To convert it into an active voice, we need to make the subject the doer of the action.
 __
 
• **Active **voice structure: Subject + verb + object__
 
 
 
• __​__In the active voice, the emphasis is on the doer of the action (someone), and the sentence is typically more straightforward and direct.
 
• In this case, "**someone**" is the doer of the action.
 
• So, the correct active voice sentence would be "*Someone called off the meeting.*"

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
**A ****sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

She will finish the thesis in a fortnight.

options.text: The thesis would be finished in a fortnight by her.
The thesis will finished by her in a fortnight.
The thesis will be finished by her in a fortnight.
A fortnight is required to finish the thesis.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'The thesis will be finished by her in a fortnight'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to **the rule of **Active and Passive voice,** when we do transition** the** tense **of the sentence **doesn't change.**
 
• Also, the** subject **of the sentence** becomes the object **and the** object **of the sentence** becomes the subject.**
 
• In the given sentence, the** subject** is** 'she'** and the **object **is** 'thesis' **and the tense is the future tense.
 
• To change it into passive voice we use **'be + V₃'**

Therefore, the** correct answer is-** *The thesis will be finished by her in a fortnight. *

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

French is taught to us by Miss Glenn.

options.text: Miss Glenn taught us French.
Miss Glenn teach us French.
Miss Glenn teaches us French.
Miss Glenn is teaching us French.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Miss Glenn teaches us French**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in passive voice, where the action is done to the subject.
 
• In **passive voice** constructions, the focus is on the recipient of the action rather than the doer of the action.
 
• **Structure**: Object (French) + Verb (is taught) + To/For Phrase (to us) + By Phrase (by Miss Glenn)__
 __
 
• **Example**: *A beautiful landscape was painted by her.*
 
 
 
• The **active voice** version will emphasize the doer of the action, bringing "Miss Glenn" to the forefront as the one performing the action.
 
• **Structure**: Subject (Miss Glenn) + Verb (teaches) + Object (us) + Complement (French)__
 
 
• **Example**: *She painted a beautiful landscape.*
 
 
 
• In the active voice, "**Miss Glenn**" becomes **the subject**, and the sentence is structured to highlight the person performing the action (**teaching**). 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The new sunshades have protected our windows during the rainy season.

options.text: Our windows are being protected by the new sunshades during the rainy season.
Our windows have been protected by the new sunshades during the rainy season
Our windows are being protected by the new windows during the rainy season.
Our sunshades have been protected by the new windows during the rainy season.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The new sunshades have protected our windows during the rainy season."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "our windows" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "have protected" to "have been protected" (present perfect passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the new sunshades."
 
• Ensure the time phrase "during the rainy season" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Our windows have been protected by the new sunshades during the rainy season."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Our windows are being protected by the new sunshades during the rainy season." – Incorrect tense (present continuous passive).
 
• **Option 3: **"Our windows are being protected by the new windows during the rainy season." – Incorrect subject ("new windows" instead of "new sunshades").
 
• **Option 4: **"Our sunshades have been protected by the new windows during the rainy season." – Incorrect subject and object swap.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Swallows build new nests every year.

options.text: New nests were built by swallows every year
New nests are built by swallows every year.
New nests were being built by swallows every year.
New nests is being built by swallows every year.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In English, passive sentences are formed by rearranging the subject, the verb, and the object of the sentence.
 
• The **object **of the active sentence** becomes** the **subject** of the passive sentence.
 
• **The verb** in the passive sentence is formed by using the appropriate form of **"to be" **plus the past participle of the main verb.
 
• In this case,** "build" **is the main verb, and its past participle is **"built."**
 
• **In the sentence** "Swallows build new nests every year", the **present simple tense **is used, which suggests a repeated or regular action.
 
• When converted into the passive voice, the same tense (present simple) should be maintained.
 
• Therefore, the **appropriate form of "to be" is "are".**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: '*New nests are built by swallows every year'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the other options:
 
 
• **New nests were built by swallows every year** - This uses the past simple tense ("were built"), so it is not the correct conversion from the original sentence, which is in the present simple tense.
 
• **New nests were being built by swallows every year** - This uses the past continuous tense ("were being built"), so it is not the correct conversion from the original sentence, which is in the present simple tense.
 
• **New nests is being built by swallows every year **- This is incorrect grammatically. "Is being built" is present continuous tense and used for ongoing actions, and the subject "new nests" is plural, which should take "are" instead of "is".

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Somebody has stolen my register.

options.text: My register has been stolen
My register has been stolen upon.
My register has stolen by somebody.
My register has been a steal.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **My register has been stolen.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• The given sentence is in **active voice**.
 
• The active voice is in **present perfect tense**.
 
• Whenever an active voice is given in present perfect tense, we change it according to the following structure:-
 
 
• Active Voice -** Subject + has/have + V₃ + Object.**
 
• Passive Voice - **Object + has/have + been + V₃ + Subject.**
 
 
 
• **For Example:-**
 
 
• Active Voice - This man **has washed** the clothes.
 
• Passive Voice - The clothes **have been washed** by this man.
 
 
 
• Here,** 'this man'**(i.e. the subject) has become the object and the **'clothes'**(i.e. the object has become the subject).
 
• In the question sentence **'my register' **is the object and** 'somebody'** is the subject.
 
• Therefore,** 'my register' **has become the subject and** 'somebody'** has become the object.

**Thus, the correct passive voice of the given active voice is** *My register has been stolen.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When we convert active voice to passive voice, three things need to be kept in mind:-

 
 
• Change object into subject.
 
• Change subject into object.
 
• Always use third form of verb in passive voice.
 
• Use 'by' before the new object.
